SETTLED IN FAVOUR OF THE CURRENT ITEM by two ABRSM primary sources, read 2026-08-09.

1. THE SYLLABUS EXAMINES A GROUPING. Grade 5 item 1 reads 'Irregular time signatures of 5/4 7/4 5/8 7/8 and the grouping of notes and rests within these times.' Source: music-theory-syllabus-outline-grades-1-5-from-2020.pdf, page 1, read as a PNG render because the metre glyphs do not extract as text (see the abrsm-syllabus-primary-source memory).

2. ABRSM MARKS ONE GROUPING CORRECT, FOR ONE MARK. The Grade 5 2020 sample paper, question 1.4: 'Tick one box to show which bar is grouped correctly.' Three engraved bars, one tick, one mark. Source: https://www.abrsm.org/sites/default/files/2023-09/music-theory-grade-5-sample-paper-200722.pdf page 3.

So the codex claim that the item should accept 3+2+2, 2+3+2 and 2+2+3 alike is wrong for an ABRSM-prep app. A grouping question has one markable answer. The e10f914 fix — ask for the NORMAL grouping, and say in the feedback that a composer may beam it otherwise — is the correct resting state and needs no further change.

ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A DEFECT. ABRSM asks the question in the opposite direction from us: it engraves three candidate bars and asks which is right, while our item asks the learner to produce the grouping. Both are defensible. If the item is ever rebuilt, the paper's shape is the one to copy.

Related: 0f835c6 added grouping:5/4 and grouping:7/4, which the same syllabus line showed were missing.

KEEP THE HEDGE. ABRSM publishes no definitions, so there is no exam gloss to match.

THE PRIMARY SOURCE IS A WORD LIST, NOT A GLOSSARY. 'ABRSM Music Theory exams: Grade 1 to 5 Terms and Signs' gives five columns of bare terms and drawn signs, with no meanings anywhere in the document. Read 2026-08-09 from the Wayback copy, because the live host gb.abrsm.org no longer resolves:
https://web.archive.org/web/20210908222304if_/https://gb.abrsm.org/media/64638/music-theory-terms-and-signs-for-grades-1-5-from-2020.pdf

So the argument in this bead that 'the exam gloss is probably slightly faster than andante' has no ABRSM document behind it. Our hedge — 'slightly faster (or slower) than andante' — is musicologically honest and nothing in the syllabus contradicts it. curriculum/terms-signs-deck.json:163 stays as it is.
